about: Studies and track records behind Hashmark's design. Each entry says what was found, why it worked (or failed), and exactly where the lesson is used in this project. 'confidence' = how well the claim is established: 'peer-reviewed', 'primary' (author's own report), 'reported' (journalism/books), or 'practitioner' (widely used, not formally tested).

studies.title: Computer Based Horse Race Handicapping and Wagering Systems: A Report
studies.venue: Reprinted in Efficiency of Racetrack Betting Markets (Hausch, Lo, Ziemba, eds.)
studies.finding: A fundamental model of horse performance was combined with the probabilities implied by public odds using a logit model. The combination beat the public odds, and Benter reports five years of profitable live betting in Hong Kong.
studies.why_it_worked: He never treated his own model as the truth. The public odds already hold most of the information, so the fitted combination only moves away from them as far as the model has earned. He also measured success as improvement over the public odds, not raw accuracy.
studies.used_in: nfl.fit_combo: logit(p) = a0 + a1*logit(market) + a2*logit(model), fitted by maximum likelihood. The backtest reports the log-likelihood gain over the market, Benter's own yardstick.

studies.title: The Combination of Forecasts
studies.authors: J. M. Bates, C. W. J. Granger
studies.finding: A weighted combination of forecasts often has lower error than any single forecast, with weights set by past performance.
studies.why_it_worked: Different forecasts make partly independent mistakes, and averaging cancels some of them.
studies.used_in: Same combination as benter-1994. The model and the market are two forecasts, and their weights are fitted on past seasons.

studies.title: A New Interpretation of Information Rate
studies.finding: Betting the fraction of bankroll that maximizes expected log wealth gives the fastest long-run growth. For a bet paying decimal odds d with win probability p: f = (p*d - 1)/(d - 1).
studies.why_it_worked: It sizes each bet by its edge, so you never bet on negative EV and you bet more when the edge is bigger.
studies.used_in: strategy.kelly_fraction_decimal and strategy.kelly_fraction_kalshi (includes Kalshi's fee in the cost).

studies.title: Good and Bad Properties of the Kelly Criterion
studies.authors: L. C. MacLean, E. O. Thorp, W. T. Ziemba
studies.venue: In The Kelly Capital Growth Investment Criterion (World Scientific)
studies.finding: Full Kelly maximizes long-run growth but can suggest very large, risky bets. Errors in the estimated edge matter far more than other errors (citing Chopra and Ziemba: errors in means vs variances vs covariances roughly 20:2:1).
studies.why_it_worked: Thorp bet a fraction of Kelly because his edge estimates were uncertain. Over-betting is punished much more than under-betting.
studies.used_in: strategy.size_bets: quarter Kelly by default, capped at 2% of bankroll per bet, 3% per game, and 10% per slate.

studies.title: Makers and Takers: The Economics of the Kalshi Prediction Market
studies.authors: Constantin Bürgi, Wanying Deng, Karl Whelan
studies.finding: Across more than 300,000 Kalshi contracts there is a favorite-longshot bias. Cheap contracts win far less often than their price implies after fees, and expensive contracts earn small positive returns. Makers (who post offers) earn more than takers (who accept them). Prices get more accurate as a market approaches its close.
studies.why_it_worked: People overpay for long shots. Patient traders who post prices are paid for providing liquidity.
studies.used_in: strategy.LONGSHOT_MIN_PRICE: Kalshi YES buys under 20 cents are never flagged. Bet notes point out that a resting limit order (maker) avoids paying the ask. Hashmark never places orders.

studies.title: Anomalies: Parimutuel Betting Markets: Racetracks and Lotteries
studies.authors: Richard H. Thaler, William T. Ziemba
studies.finding: Summarizes the favorite-longshot bias: long shots are overbet and favorites underbet, so betting long shots loses more per dollar.
studies.why_it_worked: It describes a persistent bettor bias rather than a strategy.
studies.used_in: nfl backtest 'market bias test': regresses outcomes on logit(closing market prob). A slope above 1 means favorites are underpriced. The fitted combination corrects whatever bias exists.

studies.title: Why are Gambling Markets Organised so Differently from Financial Markets?
studies.finding: Bookmakers don't simply balance action. They set prices, take positions, and shade prices to exploit predictable bettor biases, because they forecast better than bettors.
studies.why_it_worked: The bookmaker's forecasting edge plus the vig is the business model.
studies.used_in: Reason the market is a strong but not perfect benchmark: the combination is allowed to learn a bias in it (a1 different from 1). Also why the vig is always in the EV math.

studies.title: On the Probability of Winning a Football Game
studies.finding: NFL margins of victory are close to normal around the point spread, with a standard deviation of about 13.86 points (1981, 1983, 1984 seasons). A later estimate from 1978-2012 data is 13.45.
studies.why_it_worked: It turns a spread into a probability, which you need to price a spread bet.
studies.used_in: strategy.cover_prob. Our own sigma is fitted from the residuals of actual margin minus closing spread, and used for spread-bet EV.

studies.title: Does Academic Research Destroy Stock Return Predictability?
studies.finding: Across 97 published return predictors, returns were 26% lower out-of-sample and 58% lower after publication.
studies.why_it_worked: It is a warning, not a strategy. Once an edge is known, traders compete it away, and part of what looked like an edge was data mining in the first place.
studies.used_in: Walk-forward refits: each test season's weights come only from earlier seasons, and live weights are refit every season. Famous 'systems' are treated as probably decayed.

studies.title: ...and the Cross-Section of Expected Returns
studies.authors: Campbell R. Harvey, Yan Liu, Heqing Zhu
studies.finding: With hundreds of factors tested, the usual t > 2 cutoff lets through many false discoveries. A new factor should clear about t > 3.
studies.used_in: nfl.MARGIN_FEATURES and nfl.TOTAL_FEATURES are fixed in advance. A feature enters the model only if |t| >= 3 on the fit seasons. The betting simulation reports its t-statistic against the same bar.

studies.title: The Deflated Sharpe Ratio: Correcting for Selection Bias, Backtest Overfitting and Non-Normality
studies.authors: David H. Bailey, Marcos López de Prado
studies.finding: The best of many backtested strategies looks good partly by luck. The more variants you try, the higher the bar the winner must clear.
studies.why_it_worked: It counts the trials behind a result.
studies.used_in: The backtest runs a fixed set of betting variants, reports every one of them (its 'trials' count), and never picks the best threshold after the fact.

studies.title: Returns to Buying Winners and Selling Losers: Implications for Stock Market Efficiency
studies.finding: Stocks that did well over the past 3-12 months kept outperforming over the next several months (momentum).
studies.why_it_worked: Investors under-react to news, so information gets into prices slowly.
studies.used_in: Tested as the 'form' candidate feature: each team's average margin above expectation over its last 3 games. It enters the model only if it clears t >= 3.

studies.title: The Man Who Solved the Market (Renaissance Technologies / Medallion Fund)
studies.finding: Medallion reportedly returned about 66% a year before fees (about 39% after) from 1988 to 2018. It combined dozens of strategies into one system, used many weak signals that were each right only slightly more than half the time, and paid close attention to trading costs and to its own market impact.
studies.why_it_worked: Breadth (many small, mostly independent edges), costs measured carefully, constant re-testing, and risk control.
studies.used_in: Every edge here is net of vig or fee. The bet finder favors many small capped stakes over a few big ones. Stakes are capped per game and per slate. All signals are re-tested every season.

studies.title: When Genius Failed: The Rise and Fall of Long-Term Capital Management
studies.finding: LTCM made many small spread trades that looked independent, with very high leverage. In 1998 the trades all moved against it at once and the fund collapsed.
studies.why_it_worked: It's a failure: hidden correlation plus leverage turned many small edges into one large loss.
studies.used_in: Same-game legs are treated as correlated: a parlay warning and a per-game exposure cap. There is a per-slate exposure cap, and no leverage (stakes are a fraction of bankroll).

studies.title: Elo ratings (Elo 1978) and FiveThirtyEight's NFL Elo method
studies.venue: The Rating of Chessplayers, Past and Present; fivethirtyeight.com methodology
studies.finding: A simple self-correcting rating with a margin-of-victory multiplier and offseason regression to the mean forecasts NFL games reasonably well with very few parameters.
studies.why_it_worked: Few parameters means little overfitting, and it updates on every result.
studies.used_in: ratings.py: K, the margin-of-victory multiplier, 1/3 offseason regression, 25 Elo points per point of spread.

studies.title: Closing line value (CLV)
studies.venue: Widely used; we found no peer-reviewed test linking CLV to long-run profit
studies.finding: Bettors who regularly get better prices than the closing line tend to be the ones who profit over time, because the closing price holds the most information.
studies.why_it_worked: It is a faster, less noisy skill signal than win/loss records, which take thousands of bets to separate skill from luck.
studies.used_in: strategy.log_recommendations writes every recommended bet (paper trade) to data/paper_trades.csv. `python main.py clv` scores them against the nflverse closing line once games finish.
